items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The third one in line was Virgil Otto, my brother – my oldest brother.

ctx.x: Okay. We’re going to try this again. This is Bill Brower, talking with Mr. Clark Terry on June 15th for the Smithsonian Jazz Oral History Project, and we were getting background on the Terry family, and I’m going to ask if you would, to repeat the things that you told me about your parents’ background.

My mother’s name was Mary Scott. My father was Clark Terry, Sr. They had eight girls and three boys. One of the girls died before I was born, so I was raised with seven sisters and two brothers. My oldest sister Ada – Ada Mae, we called her. Next oldest in line was Marguerite Davis. She’s Davis now, but she was Terry then. Ada Mae was Ada McField. She married Sy McField. The third one in line was Virgil Otto, my brother – my oldest brother. After him came Charles Edward, whom we called Ed, my next brother. After…
You said that you just came back from St. Louis, and you received some special [?].
